newsitem.title: UK: IFC emerging market index ends 1996 up 7.0 percent.
newsitem.headline: IFC emerging market index ends 1996 up 7.0 percent.

text.p: Final figures show the International Finance Corporation's composite index of emerging market equities, denominated in dollars IFC/IPRD, rose 7.0 percent over 1996, ending the year at 295.03.
The index, which is the most commonly used means by which fund managers benchmark portfolio performance, rose 0.6 percent day-on-day after the close of trade on December 31, 1996.
Latin America edged up 0.2 percent day-on-day, and gained 14.0 percent over the year, ending at 527.97. Asia was up 1.0 percent day-on-day, and 8.9 percent over the year, at 252.77.
Europe, Middle East and Africa rose 0.3 percent day-on-day, but ended the year down 5.2 percent at 134.33.

Venezuela was the year's best performer, with final figures showing gains of 117.7 percent over 1996. Hungary came in second, rising 99.9 percent over the year, while Zimbabwe came third, climbing 72.4 percent.
The year's biggest loser was Thailand. Final figures show it down 41.1 percent over the year, followed by Korea which lost 38.7 and South Africa, which lost 19.2 percent.
The IFC composite index touched a 1996 high of 308.77 on July 4, up from the year's 275.79 low, recorded on January 1.
ING Barings' Global Emerging Market Index, also denominated in dollars BFFO, was up 0.87 percent day-on-day at 160.96 at 1000 GMT, measured after the close of play on December 31.
Over the entire year the index rose 8.9 percent. The year's high was 165.948, reached on July 3. It touched the year's 148.85 low on January 2.
Morgan Stanley's dollar-denominated Emerging Markets Free index .CEMF=USD was up 0.27 percent at 474.097, calculated after the close of trade on December 30.
It touched a 1996 high of 505.452 on July 4. The year's 458.369 low was recorded on January 1. Annual performance data was not immediately available.

All indices are capitalisation-weighted and are calculated daily. The IFC index measures returns on equities, liquid and accessible to foreign investors, from 26 emerging market countries. It is updated at 2300 GMT.
The BEMI index measures equity returns from some 20 emerging market countries, with the latest changes reported by 0900 GMT.
The MSCI Free measures equity returns from 22 emerging market nations. Changes are reported at 1300 GMT.

The J.P. Morgan emerging market bond index ELMI, its returns calculated in dollar terms, rose 0.05 percent to 124.72 by the close of trade on December 31. It gained 14.86 percent over the entire year.

By region, final figures show Latin America down 0.03 percent day-on-day, but up 31.02 over the year, at 102.27. Asia rose 0.03 percent day-on-day, and 9.03 percent over 1996, to 131.31, while East Europe climbed 0.19 day-on-day, and 17.80 percent over the year, to end at 163.08. --Caroline Brothers, London Newsroom +44 171 542 2734
